## Goal
`home()` (`src/freemyid/paths.py:9-28`, in-house) uses `%APPDATA%\FreeMyID` on Windows and `is_safe_wipe_target` (37-43) guards `freemyid wipe`. `tests/test_security_wave2.py:475` checks one non-Free-My-ID folder through the CLI; nothing tests the Windows branch or the home/root refusals directly.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. With `FREEMYID_HOME` unset, `sys.platform` monkeypatched to `win32` and `APPDATA` pointing into `tmp_path`: `home()` is `<APPDATA>/FreeMyID`, created, with the marker written (17-27). With `APPDATA` unset it falls back to `Path.home()/AppData/Roaming` (monkeypatch `Path.home` to a folder in `tmp_path`).
2. `FREEMYID_HOME` always wins over the platform branch (11-12).
3. The marker is written only into folders Free My ID created or that already hold `freemyid.db`: an existing unrelated folder named by `FREEMYID_HOME` gets no marker (20-27).
4. `is_safe_wipe_target` refuses the (monkeypatched) user home, any parent of it, the filesystem anchor of `tmp_path`, any path with two parts or fewer, and a folder with neither marker nor database; it accepts a marked folder in `tmp_path`. Nothing is created outside `tmp_path`.
5. `OWNED_ENTRIES` (31-34) includes every name the path helpers create (46-74).
6. No symlink or mode-bit assertions unless skipped cleanly where unsupported (Windows).

Fake data only (Jane Q Testperson, Springfield IL). Offline: no network, no sockets (FastAPI `TestClient` is fine), no git, no installs, no new dependencies. Tests must pass on Windows CI too: `tmp_path` and `pathlib`, no hard-coded `/tmp`, no `/`-joined path strings or other POSIX-only assumptions (WO-217 broke windows-latest that way). The module under test is outside Codex's code lane: a real product bug = `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason=...)` plus a finding with file:line in VENDOR_STATUS.md; never edit it. Check `tests/`, `tests/copilot/`, `tests/codex/` and `tests/grok/` first and don't duplicate a guard. Line numbers are from main at the time of writing; re-check them in your worktree.
